claims.sentence: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec> <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title> <jats:p>Quantify the effects of head rotation and head incline on obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity.</jats:p> </jats:sec><jats:sec> <jats:title>Design</jats:title> <jats:p>Single-arm, intervention study.</jats:p> </jats:sec><jats:sec> <jats:title>Setting</jats:title> <jats:p>Pulmonary specialty clinic.</jats:p> </jats:sec><jats:sec> <jats:title>Case presentation</jats:title> <jats:p>Ten adults diagnosed with positional OSA ranging from 32 to 64 years of age 6 females, 4 males reporting persistent daytime sleepiness and health issues with consistent use of CPAP.</jats:p> </jats:sec><jats:sec> <jats:title>Intervention</jats:title> <jats:p>Standard polysomnography with a head angle sensor attached to the forehead and coaching to fall asleep with head at various rotation and incline angles and torso in supine and non-supine positions.</jats:p> </jats:sec><jats:sec> <jats:title>Measurements</jats:title> <jats:p>OSA severity was scored according to American Academy of Sleep Medicine guidelines.
